title: Yochanan, officer of the Birah

paragraphs: Mentioned in the old Midrash Tehillim, chapter 3. Hyman says that it should undoubtedly read “Yonatan, officer of the Birah” and refers to that entry.

notes.text: The word ובל״ט remains unexplained in the frozen text; no second edition or certainty modifier is invented from it. Birah remains a designation, without identifying a capital.

The saved named OYW Midrash Tehillim chapter 3 scalar names Yochanan, officer of the Birah. It supports chapter 3 against the historical 83 guess while differing from Hyman’s proposed Yonatan correction. Supplied ובל״ט remains unresolved; conjectural ובל״ס would give “without doubt,” but no confidence modifier or second edition is silently invented. Birah remains a designation without a newly identified capital.

Hyman (vol. II, p. 694) prints ובל״ס, “without doubt,” where the supplied Hebrew has ובל״ט. The consulted Midrash Tehillim 3 first names Rabbi Yochanan, officer of the Birah, and later Rabbi Yonatan without the title. Hyman’s separate notice (p. 701) is headed Yonatan Ish HaBirah. There he reports a Yonatan reading and tentatively identifies him with Yonatan son of Elazar.
